about: Profession packs (queue profession-packs): what each kind of working life needs that a generic app misses: the licences and renewals that must never lapse, the risks and the cover that protects against them, how the income behaves and the tax route that usually fits, the next rung, and three systems that run without willpower. Paraphrased from public practice, verified on the date shown; rules differ by state, council and employer, so each pack says where to confirm. Not legal, tax or medical advice.
fields: Packs 5 to 10 (added 2026-11-16) also carry their own verified and review dates, a Global note, sources, and on a renewal: where (a country tag when the rule is one country's) and confirm (what is not verified, and who to ask). every is plain words: year, quarter, event, or a number of years.

packs.title: Salaried, private sector

renewals.t: Tax regime choice declared to the employer
renewals.how: Compare both regimes on the Savings levers card, then declare before the first payroll of the year.

renewals.t: Health cover beyond the group policy
renewals.how: Group cover ends with the job: keep a personal policy (or a top-up) in force so a job change never leaves the family uncovered.

renewals.t: Form 16 and AIS checked against your own records
renewals.how: Before filing, match salary, TDS and interest in the AIS; ask HR to correct a mismatch early.

risks.t: Sudden job loss or a restructuring
risks.cover: Six months of essential costs in the emergency fund, a personal health policy, a CV and three referees kept current.

risks.t: Income concentrated in one employer and its stock
risks.cover: Sell vested stock on a fixed rule; keep no more than a small share of net worth in the employer.

income.pattern: Steady monthly salary with yearly bonus and stock; the step-ups come from moves, not tenure.
income.tax: Salary under the cheaper regime each year; employer NPS (up to the policy share of basic) is not taxed in the new regime.

ladder: Deep skill in one area, known for one result
Leads a team or a product with a number it owns
Owns a P&L or a function
Runs a business unit or the company

systems.review: Each year: is the next rung in sight, or is it time to move?

systems.name: The money floor
systems.step: The SIP and the emergency fund move before anything is spent
systems.reward: The North Star's redundancy part rises

systems.name: Recover from long days
systems.step: A two-minute shutdown: tomorrow's one task, then off
systems.review: Sunday: energy scores of the week

packs.confirm: Your employer's HR policies and the income-tax site

packs.title: Government and public sector

renewals.t: Annual property return to your department
renewals.how: Most services ask for an annual return of immovable property by a fixed date; keep the register of assets, loans and gifts current through the year so it takes minutes. Check your service rules for the date and the form.

renewals.t: Intimation or permission before buying or selling property, or large gifts
renewals.how: Conduct rules usually require prior intimation or sanction above a value: check yours before you sign anything.
Check the NPS statement (or GPF) for every month's contribution; raise a missing credit with the drawing office early.

risks.t: Transfers and postings that split the family
risks.cover: A family plan for schooling and a second home base; keep documents scanned and shared.

risks.t: Conduct-rule breaches by accident (side income, gifts, social media)
risks.cover: A one-page list of what needs permission; ask before, never after.

income.pattern: Steady pay with dearness allowance revisions and pay commissions; pension or NPS by rule.
income.tax: Salary; the new regime often wins unless home-loan interest and other deductions are large: compare each year.

ladder: Clears the probation and the first postings with a clean record
Leads a unit; known for one reform delivered
Heads a division or a district-level charge
Policy leadership

systems.name: The asset register that writes the annual return
systems.cue: Any purchase, sale, loan or gift
systems.step: One line in the register the same day
systems.reward: The annual return is ready in minutes
systems.review: Every January, before the return is due

systems.name: Ask before you act
systems.cue: Any side income, investment in a new asset class, or public writing
systems.step: Check the one-page list; send the intimation first

systems.name: Posting-proof family life
systems.step: The relocation checklist: school, health records, address changes
systems.reward: The move takes days, not months

packs.confirm: Your service's conduct rules and the drawing and disbursing office

packs.title: Doctors and clinicians

renewals.how: Your state medical (or dental) council sets the renewal period and the CME credit points needed; keep a running CME log so renewal is a formality. Check your council's current rule.
Renew before it lapses; match the cover to your specialty's risk and keep the policy where your practice can find it.

renewals.t: Clinic registrations and licences (if you run a practice)
renewals.how: Clinical establishment registration, biomedical waste authorisation, fire safety and, where used, radiation equipment licences: each has its own renewal date.

risks.t: A malpractice claim
risks.cover: Indemnity insurance sized to the specialty, consent records kept, a lawyer known in advance.

risks.t: Burnout and irregular sleep from on-call work
risks.cover: A recovery floor (sleep, one protected day), and the daily three kept tiny on call days.

risks.t: Income that stops when you stop working (in private practice)
risks.cover: Disability income cover and a larger emergency fund than a salaried person needs.

income.pattern: Salary in a hospital; in private practice, fees that rise with reputation and stop when you stop.
income.tax: Salary, or for a practice, professional income (the presumptive route may fit small practices: confirm with a chartered accountant).

ladder: Registered and trained; the first independent cases
Known for one procedure or condition
Leads a department or a practice with its own referrals
Teaches, publishes, or builds an institution

systems.name: CME without a scramble
systems.step: One line in the CME log with its credit points and certificate

systems.name: On-call recovery
systems.step: The recovery floor: sleep first, the daily three at their smallest

systems.name: Practice compliance calendar
systems.step: Every licence and insurance renewal dated in the calendar

packs.confirm: Your state medical or dental council, and your indemnity insurer

packs.title: Licensed professionals
covers: cyber law and digital forensics experts

renewals.how: Bar council, ICAI, IAI or the Council of Architecture: each has a yearly fee or a periodic certificate; pay early and keep the receipt.
Your body sets the hours or credits (often in multi-year blocks); log each session the day you attend.
Renew before it lapses; size it to the largest engagement you sign.

risks.t: A professional negligence claim
risks.cover: Indemnity insurance, engagement letters that cap scope, and files kept for the limitation period.

risks.t: A conflict of interest or an ethics complaint
risks.cover: A conflict check before every new client, recorded.

risks.t: Uneven income between big matters
risks.cover: Pay yourself a fixed monthly draw; keep six to nine months in reserve.

income.pattern: Salary in a firm, or fees and a share of profits as a partner; lumpy when you practise alone.
income.tax: Salary, or professional income (presumptive taxation may fit up to the limit when receipts are mostly by bank: confirm with a chartered accountant); GST registration above the services threshold.

ladder: Qualified and admitted; the first matters of your own
Known for one kind of matter
Partner or practice owner with your own clients
Leads a practice area or a firm

systems.name: CPE logged as you go
systems.step: One line in the log with hours and proof

systems.name: Conflict check before yes
systems.step: The two-minute conflict check, recorded

systems.name: A fixed monthly draw
systems.step: Move the draw to the household account; the rest stays in the reserve
systems.reward: The household runs on a steady income

packs.confirm: Your bar council, institute or council, and your indemnity insurer

packs.title: Founders and business owners
covers: owners of a family or small business

renewals.t: Company yearly filing: accounts and the annual return
renewals.how: The accounts (form AOC-4) go to the registrar within 30 days of the annual general meeting and the annual return (MGT-7 or MGT-7A) within 60 days. A late form costs ₹100 a day, so date both the day the meeting is fixed. An LLP files its own two forms on its own dates.
renewals.confirm: Whether the daily late fee has a ceiling, and the LLP dates: ask your company secretary.

renewals.t: Director KYC (for anyone holding a DIN)
renewals.how: Since 31 March 2026 a director's KYC is filed once every three years, by 30 June of the year it falls due, not every year. It applies even if you sit on no board now. Update a changed phone, e-mail or address when it changes.
renewals.confirm: Your own next due year on the MCA portal: it depends on when you last filed.

renewals.t: The business tax calendar: advance tax, audit, returns, GST
renewals.how: Advance tax each quarter, the GST returns on their cycle, and the audit and return dates for the year: one calendar made each April with the accountant, not remembered.
renewals.confirm: This year's dates and whether an audit applies to you: your chartered accountant.

renewals.how: The shop or trade licence, professional tax, the import-export code's yearly update, the domain name and the trademark (every ten years): each has its own date and none sends a loud reminder.
renewals.confirm: Which of these your state and business need, and each renewal period.

risks.t: A personal guarantee on a business loan
risks.cover: Know every guarantee you have signed and its amount; keep the home and the family's savings outside the business; term cover at least equal to the guarantees.

risks.t: The business stops if you stop
risks.cover: One person who can run it for a month, written operating notes, bank access for a second signatory, key-person cover where the business can afford it.

risks.t: A cash gap between paying and being paid
risks.cover: A 13-week cash view updated weekly; a business reserve separate from the household's emergency fund.

risks.t: A dispute with a co-founder or an investor
risks.cover: A signed founders' agreement with vesting and an exit path, made while everyone still agrees.

risks.t: Household and business money mixed
risks.cover: Separate accounts from the first day and a fixed monthly pay to yourself.

income.pattern: Little or nothing for years, then irregular; most of the wealth sits in one unlisted company until a sale.
income.tax: A salary from your own company plus dividends, or business income for a proprietor or partner (a presumptive route may fit a small turnover: confirm with a chartered accountant). A share sale is taxed as capital gains.

ladder: One paying customer
Revenue that covers costs and your own fixed pay
A team that runs a week without you
Capital or profit that lets you choose: grow, sell or hold

systems.name: A fixed pay to yourself
systems.step: Move the same amount from the business to the household account
systems.reward: The household runs on a steady income

systems.name: The compliance calendar
systems.step: Every filing and renewal dated in the calendar with its owner

systems.name: The weekly cash look
systems.step: Update the 13-week cash view: what comes in, what goes out
systems.reward: You see a gap months before it arrives

packs.global: Outside India the forms differ but the pattern holds: a yearly company filing, director identity checks, a tax calendar and personal guarantees to list.
packs.confirm: Your company secretary and chartered accountant, and the MCA and GST portals

packs.title: Investors and finance professionals
covers: wealth advisers and mutual fund distributors

renewals.t: NISM certificate (the one your role needs)
renewals.how: NISM certificates such as the investment adviser levels and the mutual fund distributor exam are valid for three years. Renew before expiry through the continuing education programme or the exam (the window opens about twelve months before); once it lapses you sit the full exam again.
renewals.confirm: Which series your role needs and its renewal route: NISM and your compliance team.

renewals.t: ARN and EUIN (if you distribute mutual funds)
renewals.how: The ARN runs to the same date as the NISM certificate behind it and is renewed online with AMFI. If it lapses, commission is paid only on business brought in after the renewal.
renewals.confirm: AMFI's current circular, including the newer exam that also covers specialised investment funds.

renewals.t: Personal trading: pre-clearance and holdings disclosure
renewals.how: Your employer's code sets when you may trade, what needs approval first and how often you declare holdings (yours and close family's). Put the declaration dates and the closed-window dates in the calendar.
renewals.confirm: Your employer's code of conduct: the periods differ by firm and by role.

renewals.t: Accredited investor certificate (if you invest through that route)
renewals.how: The certificate from the accreditation agency carries its own validity date (two or three years under the 2023 rules); products bought on its strength may ask for it again.
renewals.confirm: A later SEBI circular may have changed the period: read the date on your certificate and SEBI's site.

renewals.how: A global charter or institute membership usually needs a yearly fee and a conduct declaration to stay in good standing.
renewals.confirm: Your institute's own page.

risks.t: An insider-trading or conduct breach, even by accident
risks.cover: Trade only in open windows and after approval; route family accounts through the same rule; keep every approval.

risks.t: Most of the pay is a bonus that can be deferred, cut or clawed back
risks.cover: Run the household on the fixed pay alone; treat the bonus as savings, never as budget.

risks.t: Wealth, career and employer stock all tied to one market
risks.cover: Hold the emergency fund and core savings away from your own sector; sell vested stock on a fixed rule.

risks.t: A mis-selling complaint or a regulator's enquiry
risks.cover: Written suitability notes for each client, records kept for the required years, indemnity cover if you advise in your own name.

income.pattern: A fixed salary and a large, uncertain yearly bonus; for investors, long quiet years and rare large gains.
income.tax: Salary; capital gains on your own investing, with advance tax paid in the quarter a gain arises; frequent trading may count as business income with its own audit rule (confirm with a chartered accountant).

ladder: Certified and trusted with a small book or a part of a deal
Known for one sector, product or kind of client
Runs a book, a fund or a team with its own results
A partner, or investing your own capital

systems.name: Bonus straight to savings
systems.step: Move the planned share out before spending any
systems.reward: Net worth steps up once a year by rule

systems.name: Certificates on one line each
systems.step: Add its expiry date to the calendar a year ahead
systems.reward: Nothing lapses, no exam is re-sat

systems.name: Ask before you trade
systems.cue: Any urge to buy or sell a share
systems.step: Check the window and ask for approval first

packs.global: Elsewhere the bodies change (a national regulator's licence, continuing education hours, a personal account dealing policy) but the three dates stay: licence, education hours, declarations.
packs.confirm: Your compliance team, NISM, AMFI and SEBI

packs.title: Aviation, defence and intelligence
covers: cabin crew and air traffic controllers

renewals.how: The medical is what keeps the licence usable: yearly for most airline pilots, every six months for older pilots and some single-pilot flying. Book the next one the day you pass this one.
renewals.confirm: Your exact interval by age and type of flying: DGCA's medical rules or your airline's medical cell.

renewals.how: A commercial or airline transport licence issued or renewed on or after 11 October 2023 is valid for ten years (five before that). The ratings, proficiency checks and language proficiency on it run on shorter clocks.
renewals.confirm: Each rating's and check's own date: your operator's training department.

renewals.how: The pension continues only while the yearly life certificate is current. On SPARSH the due month is your own, shown on the portal, not always November; it can be given early, digitally.
renewals.confirm: Your due date on the SPARSH portal or with your pension office.

renewals.how: Many services need permission or intimation before foreign travel, a property deal, publishing or a job after leaving. Ask before, never after.
renewals.confirm: Your service's own conduct rules: they are not public in full and differ by service.

risks.t: A failed medical ends the flying income overnight
risks.cover: Loss-of-licence insurance, health kept as a system (sleep, weight, eyes), and a second skill kept warm.

risks.t: Fatigue from rosters, night duty and time zones
risks.cover: A recovery floor after each duty; the daily three kept tiny on duty days.

risks.t: A short first career: many in uniform retire in their forties or fifties
risks.cover: A second-career plan started five years before leaving: one certificate, one network, one trial project.

risks.t: Frequent postings and long absences
risks.cover: Every family paper reachable by the partner; one fixed weekly call; schooling decisions made a posting ahead.

risks.t: Work that must stay secret
risks.cover: Keep nothing classified or operational in this app: only your own money, health, family and dates.

income.pattern: Pilots: a salary plus flying pay that follows hours flown. Uniformed services: steady pay and allowances, then a pension from an early age.
income.tax: Salary; some allowances and some pensions have their own treatment (confirm with your pay office or a chartered accountant).

ladder: Qualified: the licence, the commission or the first posting
Trusted alone: command of an aircraft, a unit or a desk
Trains and checks others
Leads the organisation, or a planned second career

systems.name: The next medical, already booked
systems.cue: The day you pass a medical
systems.step: Book the next one and put it in the calendar
systems.reward: The licence never waits on a date

systems.name: Recovery after duty
systems.cue: Wheels down, or coming off a night
systems.step: Sleep first; the daily three at their smallest

systems.name: The second-career file
systems.cue: The first Sunday of each quarter
systems.step: One small step: a course hour, a call, a page of the CV
systems.reward: Leaving becomes a choice, not a cliff

packs.global: Other countries set their own medical intervals and licence terms (each aviation authority publishes a validity table) and their own veterans' pension proofs.
packs.confirm: DGCA and your operator, your service's rules, and your pension office

packs.title: Short and uneven careers

renewals.t: Anti-doping whereabouts (athletes in a testing pool)
renewals.how: An athlete in the registered testing pool files where they will be for each quarter, with one 60-minute slot a day, and keeps it current. Three failures in twelve months (a missed test or a late or wrong filing) can count as a violation and bring a ban.
renewals.confirm: Your own filing dates and whether you are in the pool: your federation or the national anti-doping agency.

renewals.how: Every contract has an end date, a renewal window and often a clause you must act on by a date. List each with the date you must decide by, not the date it ends.
Publishers, labels and platforms send statements on their own cycle; check each against the contract and chase a missing one.
renewals.confirm: The cycle in your own contract.

renewals.t: Tax and GST for a self-employed professional
renewals.how: Advance tax each quarter on fees with no employer to deduct it in full, and GST registration once yearly receipts cross the services threshold.
renewals.confirm: The current threshold and your dates: your chartered accountant.

renewals.how: Membership often gates work, insurance or selection; pay it before it lapses.
renewals.confirm: Your body's own rule.

risks.t: An injury or illness ends the earning years
risks.cover: Personal accident and disability cover in your own name, health cover that does not depend on a team or a studio.

risks.t: A few big years must pay for a long life
risks.cover: Live on a fixed monthly pay to yourself; save most of every peak year; plan the next career before this one ends.

risks.t: A manager, agent or relative controls the money
risks.cover: Every account in your own name; you see each statement; no one else signs alone.

risks.t: No employer benefits: no provident fund, no group cover, no pension
risks.cover: Your own retirement saving by standing instruction, and your own term and health cover.

risks.t: A public mistake costs work
risks.cover: A morality clause read before signing; a two-person check before a post that could be misread.

income.pattern: A few large payments in a few years, long gaps, and an early end for many.
income.tax: Professional income. A presumptive route exists for listed professions (film artists and some sportspeople are on the list) up to ₹50 lakh of receipts, ₹75 lakh when at least 95% arrive through a bank; authors of certain books may deduct royalty up to ₹3 lakh in the old regime. The tax law was rewritten from April 2026: confirm the current section and limits with a chartered accountant.

ladder: Paid for the craft, even once
A steady run: a contract, a season, a second book
A name that brings its own offers
Income that no longer needs you on stage: rights, royalties, a business, coaching

systems.name: Pay yourself a salary
systems.step: It lands in the holding account; the same fixed pay leaves on the 1st
systems.reward: Thin months feel the same as fat ones

systems.name: Tax set aside on the day
systems.step: Move the planned tax share to its own account at once

systems.name: The decide-by list
systems.step: Add its decide-by date to the calendar

packs.global: The anti-doping rule is worldwide (the same code applies in every country). Tax relief for uneven income differs: some countries let artists and athletes average income over years; India does not.
packs.confirm: Your federation or guild, your contracts, and a chartered accountant

packs.title: Research and academia

renewals.t: Grant paperwork: the utilisation certificate and statement of expenditure
renewals.how: A government grant needs a utilisation certificate (form GFR 12-A) and a statement of expenditure for each financial year ending 31 March; the next instalment is released only after them. Start with the accounts office in March, not when the funder writes.
renewals.confirm: The date in your sanction letter and the funder's own format.

renewals.how: An approval for research with people (or animals) is not for ever: the committee asks for a progress report on its own cycle and approves any change before you make it.
renewals.confirm: The review date on your approval letter: the period is the committee's to set.

renewals.how: Under the 2022 rules a PhD takes at least three years and at most six from admission; a university may allow up to two more by re-registration, and women and scholars with a disability may get two further years. Know your last date from the first day.
renewals.confirm: Your university's ordinance: it may be stricter.

renewals.t: Fellowship, contract or visa end date
renewals.how: A fellowship, a fixed-term post and a research visa each end on a date; begin the next application nine months before.
renewals.confirm: Your award letter, contract or permit.

risks.t: A gap between grants or fixed-term contracts
risks.cover: Six to nine months of costs in reserve; two applications always in progress; one skill that pays outside academia.

risks.t: An authorship or integrity dispute
risks.cover: Authorship agreed in writing at the start; raw data and notebooks kept and dated; an image and plagiarism check before submission.

risks.t: Years of data lost
risks.cover: Three copies, two kinds of storage, one off site; a restore tried once a term.

risks.t: Who owns what you invent
risks.cover: Read the institute's IP and consulting policy before the first outside conversation.

income.pattern: A stipend or a scale salary that rises slowly; small extra income from consulting, honoraria, books and patents.
income.tax: Salary; consulting and honoraria are professional income, often shared with the institute by its rule; a scholarship for education and some royalty have special treatment (confirm with a chartered accountant).

ladder: A first paper or thesis of your own
An independent grant or a group
Known in one field: invited, cited, consulted
Builds a centre, a department or a field

systems.name: Two applications always in progress
systems.step: Open the next one the same week

systems.name: The research log
systems.cue: The end of each working day
systems.step: Three lines: what was done, where the data is, what is next

systems.name: Grant accounts in March
systems.step: One meeting with the accounts office to close the year's spend
systems.reward: The next instalment arrives on time

packs.global: Everywhere, funders tie the next payment to a report and ethics approvals expire; the forms and the doctoral time limits are each country's and each university's own.
packs.confirm: Your sanction letter, ethics committee, university ordinance and research office

packs.title: Technical specialists
covers: cloud, platform and AI engineers who hold certificates

renewals.how: 120 continuing education credits across each three-year cycle, and a yearly maintenance fee on the certificate's anniversary (reported as US$135, one fee for all your ISC2 certificates). There is no yearly minimum, but 40 a year keeps it easy.
renewals.confirm: The current fee on ISC2's own page.

renewals.how: At least 20 education hours every year and 120 across three years, plus a yearly fee; both must be reported each year. From 1 January 2027, 30 of the 120 may be outside the certificate's own subject.
renewals.confirm: The reporting date on ISACA's own page.

renewals.how: 60 professional development units in each cycle, most of them education, with a minimum in each skill area.
renewals.confirm: The cycle length and split on PMI's own page.

renewals.how: Each expires on its own date and usually renews by a shorter exam or course taken before that date.
renewals.confirm: Each vendor's page: periods differ and change.

renewals.how: Revalidated every five years under the international convention, with sea service or refresher courses and a valid medical.
renewals.confirm: The Directorate General of Shipping's current circular for your grade.

renewals.how: Valid for ten years while it is listed on the Digital Sky platform, then renewed by the regulator.
renewals.confirm: DGCA's Digital Sky page.

risks.t: The skill goes out of date faster than the career lasts
risks.cover: One skill a quarter with a finished project; a public trail of work.

risks.t: A lapsed certificate means the full exam again, or a lost contract
risks.cover: Credits logged the day they are earned; fees and expiry dates in the calendar.

risks.t: Personal blame for a sign-off (a breach, an audit, a safety failure)
risks.cover: Risks accepted in writing by the owner, not by you; ask what indemnity and insurance the employer gives your role.

risks.t: On-call and incident burnout
risks.cover: A recovery floor after an incident; a hand-over rule; leave taken.

risks.t: Contract work with gaps between engagements
risks.cover: A fixed monthly pay to yourself and six months in reserve.

income.pattern: A salary that rises with scarce skills, or day rates on contracts with gaps; seafarers earn by contract at sea.
income.tax: Salary, or professional income for a contractor (a presumptive route may fit: confirm with a chartered accountant). A seafarer's tax status depends on days spent outside India in the year: count them and confirm.

ladder: Certified and trusted with one system
The person others call for one hard problem
Owns an architecture, a programme or a function
Sets the standard: a chief, a fellow, an adviser

systems.name: Credits logged as earned
systems.cue: Any course, talk, article or event
systems.step: One line in the log with hours and proof

systems.name: One skill a quarter
systems.cue: The first Monday of the quarter
systems.step: Pick one skill and one small project that proves it

systems.name: Risk accepted in writing
systems.cue: Being asked to approve an exception
systems.step: Send the one-paragraph note naming the owner who accepts it
systems.reward: The decision sits with its owner

packs.global: The certificate bodies here are international, so the same credits and fees apply in any country; the drone and seafarer rules are each country's own under a shared convention.
packs.confirm: Each certificate body's own page, and your employer's policy on indemnity
